# Story and Acceptance Criteria Kit

> Source: PR 90 on David-Lawton-Bounteous/arc-ideation ("Story + acceptance-criteria kit for Scribl"),
> installed 2026-08-21. Mechanical changes on our copy: em dashes converted to " -- " (including the
> "Scope -- modules and files in play" heading and the V3 priority literals), links rewritten for this
> repo's layout, INSTALL.md not carried over. No design changes.

Commands, skills, and templates for running agent sessions against a backlog: how to write a
work item an agent can finish, and how to make the agent finish it without either stopping
early or wandering out of scope.

Assembled from two lines of practice: backlog management and story templating on a Jira-tracked
platform programme, and a hard-won iteration cycle on a .NET application where five or six
agent sessions ran in parallel worktrees against one board. (The rules below cap active items
at three to five: the human review queue, not the agents, proved to be the bottleneck.)

## The problem this kit solves

Agent sessions fail in two opposite directions, both from the same root cause.

- **Under-run.** The agent does the interesting part, writes a confident summary, and stops with
  two acceptance criteria unmet. The summary reads as done, so nobody rechecks.
- **Over-run.** The agent meets every criterion, then keeps going: refactors a neighbour, renames
  for consistency, grows the diff past review capacity.

The root cause is that the agent never wrote down a fixed, enumerated definition of done, so
nothing told it where the floor and the ceiling were. The fix is a four-section work-item
contract plus two enforcement skills, `acceptance-criteria-lock` and `scope-checkpoint`, that bind to
those sections literally.

> A work item is not complete until **every** acceptance criterion has recorded evidence.
> When every criterion has recorded evidence, the work item **is** complete and the session stops.

Both halves matter. The second is the one agents ignore.

## What is in here

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `template-issue-work-item.md` | The four-section contract (Jira description template; GitHub variant in the source PR's INSTALL.md). Start here; everything else binds to it |
| `template-story-v3-jira.md` | Markdown story format the Jira sync tooling parses, plus field mapping |
| `template-feature-ticket.md` | The filed backlog shape: a feature ticket's layout in Jira at intake, one stage before the four-section contract |
| `.claude/skills/acceptance-criteria-lock/SKILL.md` | Execution-time gate on *what* must be achieved. Floor and ceiling |
| `.claude/skills/scope-checkpoint/SKILL.md` | Execution-time gate on *where* the session may edit. Parallel safety |
| `.claude/skills/ears-acceptance-criteria/SKILL.md` | How to write criteria that can be gated at all, with six patterns and rewrites |
| `.claude/skills/adversarial-spec-review/SKILL.md` | Five-persona gate on whether a story is at the right level, before it goes Ready |
| `.claude/commands/start-work-item.md` | Launcher: readiness filter, collision check, one human gate, per-session brief |
| `backlog-management.md` | The board rules that changed once agents executed the tickets |
| `enforcement-gates.md` | Why prose instructions fail, and the harness mechanisms that hold |
| `team-invariants.md` | The floor the gates assume: precedence, safety, decide-or-ask, definition of done |
| `jira-filing-pipeline.md` | Gated markdown-to-Jira filing pipeline |
| `platform-jira-bitbucket.md` | The Jira + Bitbucket layer: field conventions, comment-only rule for agents, JQL, PR merge checks |

## How the pieces fit

```
template-issue-work-item.md           the contract (4 sections)
        │
        ├── written well by ──────►  .claude/skills/ears-acceptance-criteria
        │
        ├── pressure-tested by ───►  .claude/skills/adversarial-spec-review   (right level? before Ready)
        │
        ├── selected & briefed by ►  .claude/commands/start-work-item
        │                                 │
        │                                 ▼
        └── enforced at runtime by ►  .claude/skills/acceptance-criteria-lock   (what: floor + ceiling)
                                      .claude/skills/scope-checkpoint          (where: parallel safety)
                                                │
                                                ▼
                                      enforcement-gates.md       (evidence the harness checks)
                                      team-invariants.md         (the floor beneath the gates)
```

This copy is already installed; skills live in `.claude/skills/`, the command in
`.claude/commands/`. The original INSTALL.md is in the source PR. Guidance pages and
templates in this directory are reference material for the team docs or wiki.

## Adopting it (suggested order)

1. **Adopt the four sections.** Install `template-issue-work-item.md` as the Jira
   description template (GitHub variant in the source PR's INSTALL.md) and require them on every item. Keep
   the heading text byte-identical, because the skills match on it. Nothing else in the kit
   works without this step, and this step alone is worth most of the value.
2. **Add all four skill directories** under `.claude/skills/`. Have the
   session invoke `acceptance-criteria-lock` and `scope-checkpoint` as its first two actions.
3. **Optionally add the launcher** as a slash command. `/start-work-item` assumes the agent
   picks the next ready items off the board; if your team assigns work in Jira instead (a
   human puts a named item in front of a named session), skip the command entirely. The one
   piece to keep either way: whoever or whatever starts a session writes the brief with the
   four contract sections copied **verbatim**, because paraphrasing them disarms both gates
   while leaving the brief looking complete. The readiness and collision checks in the command
   are still worth stealing as a human checklist.
4. **Adopt the board rules** from `backlog-management.md`, in particular
   module-disjointness and the named shared-file list.
5. **Then, if you want it unattended,** build the Gate 1 evidence mechanism from
   `enforcement-gates.md`. Without it the AC lock rests on self-report, which works with
   a human reading the PR and does not work overnight.

## Known gap in this package

Two skill files, `acceptance-criteria-lock` and `scope-checkpoint`, exist in a production form in
a private application repository that was not reachable from the machine this package was
assembled on. **The versions here were written fresh against the documented contract those
originals bind to, not copied from them.** They are complete and self-consistent, and the
section headings match, so they are drop-in usable. If you want the battle-tested originals,
ask for the copies from the application repo's `.claude/skills/` and diff them against these.

## Provenance note

**The six-pattern EARS material is yours originally.** It came across in the harness fork on
2026-06-22 and has been in use since. What is new here, and the only part worth re-reading, is
the mandatory `Verification:` line on every criterion, the refinement quality bar, and the
vague-to-EARS rewrite table.

`adversarial-spec-review` and `team-invariants` are likewise genericised from that shared
lineage, lightly edited to drop vault-specific references and to tie their definition-of-done
language to the AC lock.

New in this kit, from the parallel-worktree application work: the four-section contract, both
enforcement skills, the backlog rules, and the launcher.

Not included, because they are tooling rather than story formation: the markdown-to-Jira sync
scripts the filing pipeline drives, a bug-filing command, and a cross-cutting bug-triage command,
all of which sit against a specific Jira project. Ask if you want them.
